cases.statement: One heterozygous carrier, patient 1 of supplementary Table S2 in 36211342: female, 37 years at interferon-signature analysis, onset in infancy, initial diagnosis SLE (recurrent fever, lymphadenitis, arthritis).

people.label: Table S2 #1
people.key_phenotypes: onset in infancy; recurrent fever, lymphadenitis, arthritis; initial diagnosis SLE; raised type I IFN score (40.3); no symptoms at sampling on prednisolone and hydroxychloroquine

quotes.quote: Table S2: Genotypes and clinical phenotypes of patients with A 20 haploinsufficiency.

phenotype_specificity.statement: Only the Table S2 entry; the initial diagnosis was SLE. The paper does not say how this patient was genotyped or whether other genes were excluded. Elevated interferon signature is reported for all HA20 patients (cohort-level).

quotes.quote: Since nine patients (from six unrelated families) in the study were diagnosed with HA20, their type I interferon signature was analyzed.

functional.statement: Construct, not patient cells: HEK293T cells transfected with pcDNA3.1+ myc-A20 'variant' constructs (the variant is named p.Lys329Asn*1) plus an NF-κB luciferase reporter, stimulated with TNF-α; suppression of NF-κB activity by the variants was significantly lower than WT (mock vector and WT as comparators; triplicate). Splicing itself was not tested in this paper.

quotes.quote: Determination of the patients’ genotypes and TNFAIP3 variants revealed several previously reported variants (32) and as well as two variants (p.Lys329Asn*1 and p.Gly583*) newly confirmed to be pathogenic using a NF-κB reporter gene activity assay (see the method of NF-κB reporter gene activity assay an Figure S2 in the electronic supplemental material).

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Canonical splice-donor substitution at intron position +1 (c.986+1G>T); the batch predicts p.? while the paper states p.Lys329Asn*1. The paper describes HA20 as caused by heterozygous loss-of-function variants.

quotes.quote: A20 haploinsufficiency (HA20) is a systemic autoinflammatory disease caused by a heterozygous loss-of-function mutation in the TNF-α-induced protein 3 (TNFAIP3).

authors_classification.statement: The authors say the variant was 'newly confirmed to be pathogenic using a NF-κB reporter gene activity assay'.

quotes.quote: Determination of the patients’ genotypes and TNFAIP3 variants revealed several previously reported variants (32) and as well as two variants (p.Lys329Asn*1 and p.Gly583*) newly confirmed to be pathogenic using a NF-κB reporter gene activity assay (see the method of NF-κB reporter gene activity assay an Figure S2 in the electronic supplemental material).

concerns: Protein differs from the prediction (batch protein_check: stated p.Lys329Asn*1, predicted p.?). The paper does not report RNA analysis, so the stated protein consequence is the authors' assumption; the reporter assay tested a cDNA construct for that assumed product, not the effect of the variant on splicing.
Numbering: 'Patient 1' in supplementary Table S2 (the HA20 carrier) is a different person from 'Patient 1 in Table 2' of the main text (a PSMB8 compound heterozygote). Use the Table S2 label only.
The variant appears only in a supplementary table converted from PDF (columns are run together in the text); no case description.
No family or parental testing reported.
No transcript stated; the batch uses NM_001270508.2.
notes_for_panel: Single supplementary-table carrier with a construct reporter assay. The key open question for the panel is the splicing consequence, which this paper does not test.
